meta.preheader: NIFTY 50 fell 1.75% to 25,349.65 on Monday as Nifty Bank lost 3.17%; foreign investors bought ₹5,673 crore (provisional); the Nasdaq fell 1.48% on Tuesday.
meta.subject: Kubeerra Market Brief · Wed 25 Nov: NIFTY 50 falls 1.75% to 25,349.65; banks down 3.17%

brief: The NIFTY 50 fell 1.75% to 25,349.65 and the Sensex 1.77% to 82,435.99 on Monday 23 Nov; Nifty Bank fell 3.17% to 62,585.35 (Upstox, Liquide, Kotak Neo). Indian markets were shut on Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti and reopen today.
Nifty Metal fell 3.68% as Tata Steel dropped 8.43% after announcing a deal with APL Apollo Tubes, whose shares fell 21.92%; Nifty IT rose 1.69% (Liquide, Angel One, Upstox).

Foreign investors bought a net ₹5,673 crore and domestic institutions sold a net ₹2,760 crore (provisional, Upstox, Kotak Neo). The rupee closed at a provisional 92.92 per dollar, 30 paise weaker (PTI).

Over India's holiday, the Nasdaq fell 1.48% and the S&P 500 0.50% on Tuesday while the Dow rose 0.85% to 50,018.70; Brent settled at $91.40 a barrel, up 2.27%, after reports of attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz (The Motley Fool, Investrade, The Nation).
IBJA's Monday afternoon rate put gold at ₹1,24,945 per 10 g, up 0.85% from Friday; on Tuesday spot gold fell about 2% to about $3,557 an ounce (IBJA, The Nation).

outlook.headline: Rate expectations, foreign buying, crude and US data frame the session after the holiday

drivers.title: Rate expectations
drivers.text: In a Reuters poll taken 13 to 20 Nov, most of 61 economists expected the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% on 4 Dec; Reuters noted that inflation rose above the upper end of the RBI's 2% to 6% band in October. Policy rates reach bank lending rates, deposit rates and bond yields.

drivers.title: Foreign buying
drivers.text: Foreign investors bought a net ₹5,673 crore on Monday and ₹1,17,622 crore from 1 to 23 November (Kotak Neo; provisional), while domestic institutions were net sellers. Flows reach large financials, the largest weight in the NIFTY 50, and the rupee.

drivers.title: Crude and the rupee
drivers.text: Brent settled at $91.40 on Tuesday, up $2.03, after reports of projectiles hitting ships near the Strait of Hormuz (The Nation); the rupee closed at a provisional 92.92 per dollar on Monday (PTI). Oil reaches India through the import bill, the rupee and fuel inflation.

drivers.title: Growth data
drivers.text: Business Standard's survey of 11 agencies puts the median estimate for July to September GDP growth at 7.7% (range 7.2% to 8.1%), against 7.8% in April to June; the data is due on 30 Nov. Growth figures shape earnings estimates and feed into the RBI's decision.

global_cues.title: US shares
global_cues.text: After India closed on Monday, the Nasdaq rose about 6.5% as Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive (Zacks); on Tuesday it fell 1.48% and the S&P 500 0.50%, while the Dow rose 0.85% (The Motley Fool). US moves reach India through foreign flows and US-exposed sectors such as IT.

global_cues.title: US yields and the dollar
global_cues.text: The US 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.90%, a two-week low, and the dollar index slipped back toward 104 on Tuesday (Trading Economics). US rates reach India through the dollar, the rupee and emerging-market flows.

events.title: US inflation and growth data
events.text: October PCE prices, the second estimate of third-quarter GDP and weekly jobless claims are due on Wednesday evening, India time (Kiplinger). Newsquawk, citing Oxford Economics, expects core PCE inflation at about 3.2% a year.

events.title: CME FedWatch shows a December Fed rise priced in
events.text: Trading Economics put the market-implied chance of a quarter-point Fed rise in December at about 95% to 97%, and The Nation said CME FedWatch showed it fully priced; Wednesday's PCE report is the next reading. The channel to India: the dollar, the rupee and foreign flows.

events.title: Ships struck near the Strait of Hormuz
events.text: Three ships were hit by unidentified projectiles on 23 Nov and Iran's Revolutionary Guards reported that a container ship hit a mine on 24 Nov (The Nation). The channel to India: the import bill, fuel inflation and the rupee.

events.title: Reported US tariff plans
events.text: Reports that the US was preparing higher tariffs on China and other countries weighed on futures and on Europe's mood (Investrade, RTTNews). The channel to India: export demand and global risk appetite.

commentary.text: IBJA published no rates on 24 Nov, so its Monday rates do not yet reflect Tuesday's fall in international prices.
The Nation said gold and silver fell as traders fully priced a December rise in US rates; higher rates raise the cost of holding metals, which pay no interest.
Fawad Razaqzada of FOREX.com said falling share prices had forced some investors to sell gold and silver to meet calls for more collateral (The Nation).

stories.headline: RBI proposes a 'stop switch' for digital payments
stories.what: The RBI released draft directions on 23 Nov under which customers could block all new digital debits at once, turn individual channels off and on, and name a trusted person to approve transfers above a threshold, a check that would not apply to UPI, merchant or recurring payments. Comments are due by 14 Dec (ANI via The Tribune).
stories.why: The drafts would change how banks and payment providers handle digital fraud; they are proposals and not yet in force.

regulatory.text: From 1 April 2027, a scheme may net its payments for shares bought against receipts for shares sold in the same settlement cycle, for outright cash market trades within each scheme only; securities still settle trade by trade (SEBI circular).

category_explainer.text: Under SEBI's scheme categories, as revised in February 2026 and reported by Upstox, a gilt fund is an open-ended debt scheme that keeps at least 80% of its money in government securities across maturities; a 10-year constant maturity gilt fund keeps the same minimum and a portfolio Macaulay duration of 10 years. Morningstar India notes that government securities carry very little credit risk, but their prices move with interest rates, so these funds' NAVs can change noticeably when yields move. Each scheme's riskometer level and risk factors are in the fund house's own documents.

learn.title: What a 1:1 bonus issue changes, and what it does not
paragraphs: A bonus issue gives existing shareholders extra shares free, in proportion to what they hold. The company funds it by moving money from its free reserves or securities premium into share capital, so no cash leaves the company (Upstox learning centre).

In a 1:1 bonus, each share held on the record date earns one more, so the number of shares doubles. The share price adjusts on the ex-bonus date in the same proportion, so the total value of a holding is unchanged on that day: 100 shares at ₹500 become 200 shares at ₹250 (Upstox learning centre).

Tech Mahindra has set 30 Nov as the record date for its 1:1 bonus, subject to shareholder approval, with the new shares tradable from 2 Dec (Upstox News). A bonus changes the count of shares, not the value of the business.
